kurzbeschreibung: Kufstein and the **Wilde Kaiser** – one of Tirol’s most stunning mountain backdrops, featuring the fortress of Kufstein and the majestic **Kaisergebirge**.
beschreibung: The **Kufstein & Wilder Kaiser** region stretches along the lower Inn Valley up to the German border. The medieval **Festung Kufstein** fortress dominates the city majestically and serves as the region’s landmark. The **Kaisergebirge**—comprising the Wilder Kaiser and Zahmer Kaiser—is one of the most distinctive mountain ranges in the Eastern Alps. **St. Johann in Tirol** and **Ellmau** are well-known holiday destinations with direct access to the Wilder Kaiser–Brixental ski area. **Söll** blends tradition and modernity at the heart of the ski resort. **Alpbach** has been repeatedly named Austria’s most beautiful village. The medieval **Rattenberg**, with just 400 inhabitants, is Austria’s smallest town.
tipps: Die Festung Kufstein bietet die größte Freiorgel Europas – das Heldenorgel-Konzert täglich um 12 Uhr.
Alpbach ist besonders im Herbst sehenswert – der Dorfkern mit seinen typischen Balkonhäusern ist einzigartig.
Das Skigebiet Skiwelt Wilder Kaiser–Brixental ist Österreichs größtes zusammenhängendes Skigebiet.
empfehlungen: A must: Climbing up to the **Festung Kufstein** for a panoramic view over the Inntal. Afterwards, a hike in the **Kaisergebirge** to the **Stripsenjochhütte** – one of the most beautiful day-trip destinations in the region.
umgebung: The **Kufstein** region borders **Bayern** (Germany) to the north, **Salzburger Land** (**Saalbach**) to the east, and the **Kitzbüheler Alpen** to the south. Neighboring regions include **Kitzbühel** (south), **Zillertal** (west), and **Achensee** (southwest). The fortress town of **Kufstein** lies just 10 km from the German border.
